CHAPTER.VERS: Why, seeing times are not hid from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days?

remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and their feed.
feed…: or, feed them
They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
They turn the needy out of the way: the poor of the earth hide themselves together.
Behold, wild donkeys in the desert, they go forth to their work; rising early for a prey: the wilderness food for them for children.

They reap his grain in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.
corn: Heb. mingled corn, or, dredge
they gather…: Heb. the wicked gather the vintage
They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that no covering in the cold.
They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.
They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.
They cause to go naked without clothing, and they take away the sheaf the hungry;
make oil within their walls, tread winepresses, and suffer thirst.
Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly .
They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not its ways, nor abide in its paths.
The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief.

The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth face.
disguiseth…: Heb. setteth his face in secret
In the dark they dig through houses, they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.
For the morning to them even as the shadow of death: if knoweth the terrors of the shadow of death.
He swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards.

Drought and heat consume the snow waters: the grave have sinned.
consume: Heb. violently take
The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and wickedness shall be broken as a tree.
He wrongeth the barren beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow.

He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no is sure of life.
no…: or, he trusteth not his own life
it is given him in safety, on which he resteth; yet his eyes upon their ways.

They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all , and cut off as the tops of the heads of grain.
are gone: Heb. are not
taken…: Heb. closed up
And if not now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech of no worth?
